title: Manual Lock Acquisition and Release (Non-RAII)
pattern: Manual calling of explicit lock/unlock methods without an RAII guard, or putting lock() inside a try-catch block.
why_bad: If an early return, panic, or exception occurs during do_work(), the lock is leaked, causing immediate deadlock in subsequent threads. Putting lock() inside try blocks can cause unlock() to be called on an unacquired lock, causing undefined behavior.
detection: Observe direct calls to mutex.lock() and mutex.unlock() (or equivalent) in the same function scope instead of using an RAII-style guard or scope-based locking wrapper.
counterexample: Using an RAII lock guard like std::unique_lock in C++ or mutex.lock().unwrap() in Rust which releases the lock automatically on drop.
fix: Use an RAII guard: `let _guard = lock.lock().unwrap();` or `std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mutex);` to guarantee release.
source: Herlihy, p. 141-142 [157]; or [Addison-Wesley Professional Computing Series] Richard L. Sites - USD, p. 102 [876-877].
